_about: Caveats and discrepancies table of the 3D models tab (one row per discrepancy, across models). Written 2026-10-06 from METHODS_3D.md sections 4, 5, 7 and the bathymetry REPORT.md files; 'ev' snippets are checked against the documents at build time. Models without rows here get auto-extracted rows from the Limitations table of their METHODS_3D.md (marked 'auto'). 'section' = where the row is explained in that model's METHODS_3D.md; 'status' is one of: resolved | open | unresolved | by-design.

rows.model: 443 m3 (state B), 550 m3 (state A)
rows.stated: 110 bags: 695-782 m3 at 80-90 % fill, 869 m3 nominal (110 x 7.9 m3) - Borrero & Nelsen 2003 pp.2-3; Borrero et al. 2010 p.7
rows.diff: -252 to -339 m3 (-36 to -43 %) vs filled; -426 m3 (-49 %) vs nominal
rows.reason: Stack height / number of courses is not stated by any source; the 110 bags (703 m2 of bag footprint) cannot lie in one layer inside the 435.2 m2 traced outline; bags may have been less full. A second course at the apex is not supported (V12).
rows.resolve: As-built cross-sections or photographs of the stacks; Coastal Frontiers 2008 removal mapping; the survey files of the 2003 paper
ev: 110 bags: 869 m3 nominal, 695-782 m3 at 80-90 % fill; model B = 443 m3
V8/V9 are an unresolved discrepancy, not a pass.

rows.q: Crest level: design vs as installed
rows.model: B (default) -2.678 m MSL at the apex; A -1.829 m MSL
rows.stated: design drawing 'TOP OF BAG MIN DEPTH -6' MSL'; paper 'approximately - 6 ft MLLW' (p.2)
rows.diff: 0.849 m = MSL - MLLW
rows.reason: The same number (6 ft) carries two datum labels (MSL on the drawing, MLLW in the paper); the paper does not say which is right. Crest B (crest A in the earlier runs) is the only as-built value; the design crest A stays selectable.
rows.resolve: As-built survey or dive depth-gauge records mentioned in the paper
ev: A and B are the same number (6 ft) with different datum labels

rows.stated: text: '200 m south of the 1-mile outfall' (but the same paper's Fig. 2 reads about 340 m from the outfall and 670 m from the Grand Street jetty); earlier CCC hint 217 m away; jetty-based estimate 160 m further north
rows.diff: the three estimates span 190 m
rows.reason: No georeferenced outline exists; the position is the centre of the Fig. 9 survey window of the 2003 paper. Depths are barely affected (seabed uniform alongshore, sd 0.14 m), the picture is.
rows.resolve: Google Earth Pro historical imagery 2001-2008; raw survey files
ev: outfall- and jetty-based estimates span 190 m; +-150 m decided 2026-10-10

rows.model: -3.67 m MSL (NOAA DEM)
rows.stated: five other estimates from -2.92 (CRM) to -5.00 m (RWR 'about 5 m deep', datum unstated); Navionics -3.02 m
rows.diff: -0.75 m to +1.33 m; sample SD 0.83 m
rows.reason: Reef distance from the waterline is uncertain (+-25 m x slope 1:32 = 0.78 m); DEM cells are 10 m and composite (1932-2009); Navionics datum assumed MLLW and counting carries +-2 lines.
rows.resolve: High-resolution lidar/multibeam; Navionics app readings
ev: sample SD of six estimates (0.83 m

rows.q: Profile axes of the paper's Figs 5 and 7/8
rows.model: used only for cross-checks, not for model numbers
rows.stated: Fig. 5 = Fig. 7 + 1.44 m vertically and about 5.5 m horizontally; vertical datum not stated
rows.diff: 1.44 m datum ambiguity (MHW - MLLW 1.43 m or MSL - LAT 1.47 m)
rows.reason: Datum and units of the paper's Figs 5-9 are not stated; Fig. 5 read as MLLW (zero line 'Approx. Min Low Tide').
rows.resolve: The authors (J. Borrero, C. Nelsen) or the raw survey files
ev: Fig. 5 = Fig. 7 + 1.44 m vertically

rows.model: Phase I as built (110 bags, design footprint)
rows.stated: after Phase II: relief 2.12 m, base width 29.4 m at the centreline (design apex block 10.6 m)
rows.diff: the widened Phase II reef was about three times as wide
rows.reason: Phase II (+90 bags over Phase I, April 2001) and the erosion to 2002 are deliberately not modelled; the Phase I profile is not available (the Nov 2000 profile stops at d = 109 m).
rows.resolve: Feb 2001 / Oct 2000 survey lines
ev: the widened Phase II reef was about three times as wide

rows.model: 13,119 m3 (idealised loft)
rows.stated: about 13,000 m3 (Mead et al. 2010)
rows.reason: Agreement, within the parameter ranges (slope 1:2 / 1:3 / 1:4 gives 14,184 / 13,119 / 12,161 m3). The April 2011 survey relief (9,573 m3) is the damaged state; the design relief of Fig. 3a gives 11,540 m3.
ev: loft 13,119 m3 against about 13,000 m3 stated (+0.9 %)

rows.q: Vertical datum of the Fig. 9 survey (the weakest link)
rows.model: survey zero = chart datum (ACD); z_MSL = z_ACD - 1.40
rows.stated: Rendle & Davidson p.8: 'MSL is equivalent to Chart Datum, Newlyn' (garbled; not used)
rows.diff: +-1.4 m on every absolute height if the zero were Ordnance Datum (relief unchanged)
rows.reason: The authors do not state the datum. Evidence for ACD: crest +0.05..+0.65 m vs design +0.5 m ACD; '2.7 to 5 m depth'; upper section exposed at low springs; EMODnet closer to ACD than to ODN. The viewer has an alternative-datum switch.
rows.resolve: Rendle PhD thesis (Plymouth), CCO survey metadata, or the Navionics app datum setting
ev: **A3** The depth axis of Fig. 9 is referred to chart datum (ACD).

rows.model: Fig. 9 + spline seabed (April 2011 DGPS)
rows.stated: EMODnet minus model = -1.8 +- 0.7 m (7 cells; reef-centre cell -1.39 m, n = 12 cells -1.14 / -1.39 / -1.30 m)
rows.diff: EMODnet 1.8 +- 0.7 m deeper (not a constant shift)
rows.reason: Cells (116 x 73 m) are larger than the reef; shallow-limit sampling bias of the source survey (CDI 117452) or a datum labelled LAT but effectively ODN (then the difference is +0.18 m for the n = 12 cells). The DTM does not show the reef. EMODnet carries about +-1.5 m of datum and sampling uncertainty and does not override Fig. 9 + Navionics.
rows.resolve: Vertical datum of CDI 117452 (EMODnet CDI page); a finer UK survey (CCO, UK Civil Hydrography Programme)
ev: -1.8 +- 0.7 m over 7 cells
EMODnet absolute levels at Boscombe carry about +-1.5 m of datum and sampling uncertainty

rows.stated: literature 'about 1 ha'
rows.reason: The traced outline of the bag field (2011-09-28 image) agrees with two other plan-view sources; 1 ha would need only 1.3 m mean thickness, which does not fit two layers of 1-5 m containers.
ev: The text "about 1 ha" would need 1.3 m of mean thickness

rows.model: flat +0.5 m ACD along the whole outline
rows.stated: Oct 2009 profile tops +0.05 to +0.65 m ACD (typically +0.2 to +0.3); April 2011 maximum +0.68 m; unverified snippet: final crest 0.5 m above the final design height
rows.diff: +-0.3 m (up to +0.5 m if the unverified snippet is right)
rows.reason: The 'focus' and 'wedge' sections have different design heights and are not published; settlement 0.5 m or less; the model is an idealised flat crest.
rows.resolve: Oct 2009 survey grid, Rendle thesis, CCO data request
ev: The final crest height of Boscombe ASR was 0.5 m higher than the final design height

rows.model: April 2011 survey zones: drying 296 m2, <0.5 m 956 m2, <1 m 1,609 m2
rows.stated: SonarChart 378 / 950 / 1,630 m2; Nautical Chart 492 / - / 2,073 m2
rows.diff: within 1-2 % at the 0.5 m and 1 m levels; drying patch +82 to +196 m2
rows.reason: Navionics shows the damaged but still present structure; the SonarChart keeps older chart data for drying areas, so it is not fully independent of the survey; chart datum not stated by the app.
rows.resolve: Navionics app datum / tap on the drying area
ev: 16 soundings on seabed inside the model grid

rows.model: as installed Dec 2019, torn before completion; verdict FAILED
rows.stated: developer (Waveco 2025): 'In 2018, we deployed ... It wasn't a failure'
rows.diff: year contradicted (Dec 2019); waves not independently supported
rows.reason: Every dated 2019 report (ABC, Tracks, RWR, The Inertia, SurferToday, forum observer) places the installation in December 2019; Tracks (2021) reports that the developer 'readily admits' the first trial failed. Waveco's '2018' date is rejected; no developer claim overrides the verdict.
ev: The verdict stays FAILED
Waveco's "2018" versus the record.

rows.model: 0.38 m (H = 2.0 m) to 0.78 m (H = 1.6 m) below MLLW; Monte Carlo 0.69 +- 0.66 m
rows.stated: 'about 1m under the surface at low tide' (RWR)
rows.diff: model 0.62 m shallower at H = 2.0 (0.9 sigma)
rows.reason: 'Low tide' is undefined in the source (MLLW assumed; LAT would be 0.4 m lower); the position (30-50 m) and height (1.6-2.0 m) ranges move the crest by about 0.4-0.8 m.
rows.resolve: RWR / Waveco design document; installation photos
ev: crest depth below MLLW of 0.69 m with sd 0.66 m

rows.q: Seabed depth vs the text-implied seabed
rows.stated: -3.20 m AHD (H = 2.0) or -2.80 m (H = 1.6) from 'crest 1 m under low tide + height'
rows.reason: About one sigma of the seabed estimate (0.61 m); the lidar reaches the text-implied depth at y = 42-50 m, inside the text range 30-50 m. Lidar is 10 years older than the installation (sigma_change 0.30 m assumed).
rows.resolve: Newer survey; Navionics app readings
ev: differences at the default 0.62 m (H = 2.0) and 0.22 m (H = 1.6)

rows.model: 2.0 m default (1.6-2.0 m), symmetric spherical cap
rows.stated: 2 m (ABC, RWR) vs 1.6 m (Tracks); 'skateboard ramp' profile (Tracks 2021)
rows.diff: 0.4 m between sources
rows.reason: All heights are pre-install design figures; the real bladder was partly filled, unanchored and torn, so its surface was lower and flatter in places. No cross-section of the installed bladder exists.
rows.resolve: Waveco / Bottegal installation photos or dive survey; City of Bunbury incident records
ev: the cap may be taller/flatter than the real bladder by 0.3 m or more

rows.q: Sand fill mass vs cap volume
rows.stated: 140-150 t of sand (developer only) = 70-94 m3 settled
rows.diff: sand fills 60-80 % of the H = 2.0 m cap (101 % of a 1.6 m cap at 150 t, dry density)
rows.reason: Own arithmetic with assumed bulk densities (1.6 dry, 2.0 saturated); the 140 vs 150 t gap (7 %) is below the density uncertainty (about 25 %). Not used by the model.
rows.resolve: independent weighing (none)
ev: is physically credible; a mostly sand-filled bladder

rows.model: datum inferred = LAT (-0.60 m AHD) by RMS against the 2009 lidar
rows.stated: app states no datum; RMS 0.32 m (LAT), 0.67 (MLLW), 0.87 (AHD), 0.96 m (MSL)
rows.diff: mean difference lidar - chart +0.25 m at y = 30-150 m
rows.reason: LAT is the best fit; MSL and AHD are rejected; MLLW is disfavoured, not excluded (0.4 m higher). Structure not visible in the chart.
rows.resolve: Navionics app settings and readings
ev: LAT best; MSL/AHD rejected

rows.q: Volume and height vs the council register
rows.model: envelope 22,000 m3; crest height above the seabed 3.9 m (max 4.17 m)
rows.stated: City of Gold Coast asset register VOLUME 33,000 and HEIGHT_M 5 (units and reference not stated); 25,000 m3 'quarried rock' (ICM / Salyer 2024); 60,000 t placed (EPW 2020)
rows.diff: -11,000 m3 (-33 %) and -1.1 m (-22 %) vs the register
rows.reason: Not explained: the register may carry design or pay-line quantities, rock below the original seabed (toe trench, settlement), or the contour interval may exceed 0.5 m on the crest side. The register volume is reproduced only with a seabed 1.0 m deeper than all independent seabed evidence. 60,000 t / 33,000 m3 = 1.82 t/m3 is a normal placed-rock bulk density.
rows.resolve: City asset team (meaning of HEIGHT_M and VOLUME); as-built multibeam / Design Reference Report
rows.ids: s1; n1; s7; Gold Coast report 5.3
ev: The model envelope is 33 % below the register envelope.
The register's 5 m / 33,000 m3 lies 2.0 sigma (height) and 1.8 sigma (volume) above the model.

rows.model: design crest -1.5 m MSL = 0.62 m below LAT
rows.stated: nautical chart label 'FISH HAVEN 1.5MT' (datum not stated by the app)
rows.diff: 0.88 m if the chart depth is below LAT (chart top deeper than the design)
rows.reason: The chart figure equals the design number, which suggests it was copied without a datum conversion (datum ambiguity MSL vs LAT = 0.88 m). The model uses the design value (four sources) and records the difference.
rows.resolve: Navionics app tide note and readings (REQUESTS A1, A2)
ev: The figure 1.5 equals the design number, which suggests it was copied without a datum conversion.

rows.q: Concept design vs the built reef
rows.model: as-built: 162 x 91 m, 11,972 m2, crest -1.5 m
rows.stated: Mortensen et al. 2015 concept: 175 x 144 m, 21,394 m2, 53,319 m3, offshore toe 560 m from shore in 11.4 m
rows.diff: concept is 78 % larger in area and 2.4 x in volume (not built)
rows.reason: Detailed design (Royal HaskoningDHV) moved the reef about 50 m shoreward and reduced it to about 160 x 80 m. The concept is used only for the slope labels (1/12, 1/5) and as context; its volume is not a stated volume of the built reef.

rows.q: Datum: AHD vs MSL and the tide planes
rows.model: z_MSL = z_LAT - 0.88 (Gold Coast Seaway planes)
rows.stated: concept crest '-1.5 m AHD' vs built '1.5 m below MSL'; MSQ: AHD is 0.760 m above LAT at the Seaway benchmark (MSL = AHD + 0.12 m); Palm Beach interpolated MSL - LAT about 1.0 m (0.88-1.09)
rows.diff: 0.12 m (AHD vs MSL); crest about -0.50 m LAT instead of -0.62 m LAT if MSL - LAT = 1.0 m
rows.reason: MSQ has no Palm Beach row (the Seaway is 18 km away, Snapper Rocks 10 km with MSL 1.09 m above LAT). The METHODS note now carries the AHD offset as verified (MSQ 2014, read at the source by the Gold Coast bathymetry report; updated in the 2026-10-10 re-check); it applies at the Seaway benchmark only.
rows.resolve: Local tide table / MSQ interpolation

rows.q: Seabed and reef surface are inferred, not surveyed
rows.model: seabed from the Navionics SonarChart; surface from 10 unlabelled aerial contour lines at an assumed 0.5 m interval
rows.stated: contour interval regressed 0.459 +- 0.003 m (formal); toe elevation vs chart seabed -0.27 m (sd 0.55 m); pre-reef City survey profile (Mortensen 2015 Fig. 6a) agrees with the chart to 0.2-0.3 m RMS after the LAT to AHD/MSL shift and with the model seabed to 0.33 m RMS (13 labels, AHD assumed); PBO3 buoy (Daniels 2022) 11.75 m vs model 12.37 m below LAT (+0.62 m, extrapolated beyond the 10 m line); City DTM has no open-coast seabed
rows.diff: interval +9 % (assumed 0.5 vs 0.459); toe 0.27 m deeper than the chart
rows.reason: With a 1.0 m interval the seaward toe would be at -12.5 m, 5 m below the chart. Absolute depth and height are +-0.5 m; no surveyed depth value was read.
rows.resolve: As-built multibeam (City of Gold Coast); Navionics app readings A1-A7
ev: With 1.0 m the seaward toe would be at -12.5 m MSL, 5 m below the chart.

rows.q: Offshore seabed (y 380-650 m): alongshore tilt (D2 applied)
rows.model: row y = 380 and everything seaward flat alongshore (alongshore mean -7.78 m MSL, EMODnet cross-shore gradient 0.0141); r.m.s. 0.51 m against 11 Navionics soundings (was 1.20 m)
rows.stated: Before D2: EMODnet DTM 2024: no alongshore gradient; Navionics soundings: model -1.2 m per 100 m of x too deep at x < 0 and too shallow at x > 0 (up to +-1.7 m)
rows.diff: r.m.s. 1.20 m before, 0.51 m after D2 (2026-10-10)
rows.reason: Before D2 the extension copied the spline row y = 380 (tilt +0.76 m per 100 m of x) to y = 650. D2 flattened it. The zone is context for the shoreline and does not touch the reef or the survey cells. The step between rows 378 and 380 at the x edges is 1.13 m; the 11 hand-read soundings still show -0.44 m per 100 m of x.
rows.resolve: Applied 2026-10-10 (D2); reversible with 3d/archive/pre_D2/.
ev: Since D2 (2026-10-10) row y = 380 and all rows seaward are set to the alongshore mean

rows.model: beach = CCO profile surface of 2010-04-20 (11 lines, m ODN taken as m MSL); viewer draws the waterline of the selected level plus the 2011-09-28 surf line y = 0 (z -0.2 m)
rows.stated: the traced image is of 2011-09-28 (tide state unknown); beach variability date to date 0.1-0.5 m
rows.diff: a level error of 0.35 m moves a waterline by about 9 m
rows.reason: The CCO survey after completion and before the 2011 failure is the nearest date with all 11 lines; ODN is taken as MSL within +-0.1 m (A4).
rows.resolve: A beach date nearer to autumn 2009 exists on 2 lines only; ask Lior if another date is wanted.

rows.model: {{versions/multibeam_2013_m2p0/volume_m3_default|n0}} m3 default / {{versions/asr_installed_toe_2008/volume_m3_default|n0}} m3 toe loft at the default bed {{seabed/bed_default_cd|d1}} m CD
rows.stated: 2,800 m3 built volume (Raised Water Research, BoPRC p28); Installed grid 2,835-2,861 m3
rows.diff: {{= (P('versions/multibeam_2013_m2p0/volume_m3_default') / P('stated_volume_m3') - 1) * 100 |s0}} % / {{= (P('versions/asr_installed_toe_2008/volume_m3_default') / P('stated_volume_m3') - 1) * 100 |s0}} % vs 2,800 m3; reproduced at a bed of {{versions/multibeam_2013_m2p0/bed_for_2800_m3|d2}} / {{versions/asr_installed_toe_2008/bed_for_2800_m3|d2}} m CD
rows.reason: Volume = sum of crest-to-bed height over the footprint. The bed under the reef in 2008-09 is not measured; every later source reads it shallower than -4.0 m CD (at -4.0 the model was +15 % (toe) to +29 % (survey outline) over the stated figure). Decision D1 of Lior (2026-10-07), applied 2026-10-10: default bed -3.6 m CD, labelled an ASSUMPTION; option 'later seabed' -2.8 m CD (about 1,750 m3, 37 % below 2,800 m3; P2 Fig 12, Oct 2006, reads the bed beside the reef at 2.0-3.7 m). P3 (Mead & Borrero 2011) Fig 3: 2,800 m3 of the 6,500 m3 design volume was in place (METHODS_3D 4.3).
rows.resolve: An as-built bed survey, or the datum of the ASR 'Installed' image or a scaled as-built section (REQUESTS_FOR_LIOR).
ev: Stated as built 2,800 m3 (RWR / BoPRC p28); Installed-grid 2,835-2,861

rows.q: As-built bed level (the 3 m height depends on it)
rows.model: {{seabed/bed_default_cd|d1}} m CD default (ASSUMPTION), selector {{= ', '.join('%.1f' % v for v in P('seabed/bed_options_cd')) }} m CD, plus a later-seabed option
rows.stated: BoPRC p23 3.0-4.0 m (2008); consent 3.7-4.6 m; design 4.5 m; Scarfe 2007 about 2.8-3.0 m; 2013 survey 2.4-3.3 m; Navionics 2026 {{seabed/z_nav_at_reef_cd|d2}} m (m CD)
rows.diff: {{= abs(P('seabed/bed_default_cd') - P('seabed/z_nav_at_reef_cd')) |d2}} m from the 2026 chart at the centre
rows.reason: No source measured the 2008-09 bed at the reef; the ASR Installed image shows it but its datum is unstated. The default is a labelled assumption, not a finding; height, flank width and volume all follow it (+-0.5 m of bed = about +-19 % of volume).
rows.resolve: D1 applied 2026-10-10 (default -3.6 m CD ASSUMPTION, option -2.8 m CD). Settled only by the datum of the ASR 'Installed' image or a scaled as-built section (REQUESTS_FOR_LIOR).

rows.model: {{versions/multibeam_2013_m2p0/area_m2|n0}} m2 default (-2.0 m CD contour, 2013); {{versions/asr_installed_toe_2008/area_m2|n0}} m2 toe (2008 as-built); aerial dark mass 1,723 m2 (area only, not drawn)
rows.stated: Scarfe 2008: reef area 2,400 m2 at 70 % complete; BoPRC '80 x 70 m'
rows.diff: up to 2x between definitions
rows.reason: The four numbers use different edge definitions (contour, toe, dark mass in an aerial, design). Text sizes are not used to scale anything.
rows.resolve: Switch the outline version in the model header; the viewer labels each edge definition.

rows.model: 1:1 skirt from the -2.0 m contour to the bed (slider 0.25-2) in the default version; linear loft from the toe in version 2
rows.stated: no section drawing exists; the toe lies a median 0.56 m (90 % 2.83 m) outside the -2.0 m contour
rows.reason: Flanks of the as-built bags were steeper than 1:1 (the toe outline implies it), so the default skirt over-states the footprint at the bed and the volume.
rows.resolve: An as-built section (Mead et al. 2007 / 2011).

rows.model: as-built delta wing (mid-2008), apex bags drawn intact at the main crest
rows.stated: BoPRC: apex bags deflated by Jul 2013; bags removed 25 Sep to 8-9 Nov 2014 (SunLive); fabric ashore 18 Jan 2023
rows.reason: The reef no longer exists. Later states are caption and history only, never drawn; the buried base bags of the north arm appear in the toe version only.

rows.q: Seabed outside the reef (2026 chart, not the 2008 seabed)
rows.model: Navionics SonarChart 2026 read on 5 shore-normal transects, alongshore uniform, shifted to the bed with a ramp; schematic 1:15 dry beach for y < 0; scour hole in the V not modelled
rows.stated: scour hole -4.9 m CD (2013), -6.4 m CD (2008-09), 7,500 m2 (Scarfe)
rows.reason: SonarChart is crowd-sourced, undated and not for navigation; its datum is not stated by the viewer (read as chart datum and tested against the 2013 multibeam bed: r.m.s. 0.30 m as CD, 0.78 as MVD-53, 0.95 as MSL).
rows.resolve: Navionics app depth read at the reef centre and the 2.4 m sounding (REQUESTS_FOR_LIOR 5).

rows.q: Vertical datum (z = 0 at present mean sea level)
rows.model: z = 0 = MSL = CD + 1.13 m (LINZ Tauranga 2006-2025); CD = z -1.13 m; MVD-53 = z -0.168 m
rows.stated: Scarfe / ASR heights are MVD-53 ('MSL 1953') = CD + 0.9622 m
rows.diff: 0.17 m between the two mean-sea-level definitions
rows.reason: Heights quoted in MVD-53 or CD were converted; both datum lines are drawn so a reader can see the difference.

rows.model: {{versions/lidar_2022/volume_m3|n0}} m3 laser edge / {{versions/design_1020/volume_m3|n0}} m3 design foot / {{versions/sat_2024/volume_m3|n0}} m3 photo edge (+-4,600 m3 for 0.4 m of bed)
rows.stated: no reef-only quantity at a primary source; Type 4 for the whole Phase 1: 42,000 t (NCE)
rows.diff: default Type 4 layer about 36,100 t, below 42,000 t
rows.reason: Volume = crest surface minus the modelled seabed. Only the bed under the rock matters, and it is a design level (-4.0 mODN derived); the three outline versions differ by up to 15 %.
rows.resolve: A reef-only rock quantity from the contractor; a low-tide multibeam or imagery of the flanks below -2.3 mODN.

rows.q: Offshore seabed (y > 335 m) versus the Fig 2 -4.0 m contour
rows.model: follows the Fig 2 -4.0 m contour (traced nodes, plus assumed bridge and extension nodes); beyond it the EMODnet gradient -1.1 % (mODN)
rows.stated: HRPP576 Fig 2: -4.0 m contour at y 410-460 m; EMODnet cells 0.7-1.2 m shallower; Navionics chart zero -3.58 mODN
rows.diff: 0.00 m at the 13 traced points (was 0.89 m deeper before the D6 fix of 2026-10-07)
rows.reason: The first build evaluated the seabed fit at y <= 335 m only and used an assumed -4.0 m anchor there, so it ignored the Fig 2 -4.0 m contour and the design bed nodes under the arm head. The D6 fix (option B) makes the contour a control; the bed under the arm head rose up to 0.7 m and the rock volumes fell 3.4-3.9 %.
rows.resolve: Done (D6, 2026-10-07). Remaining: the -4.0 m level is bridged / extended by assumption at x -104..170 and x > 170; a sounding line or multibeam seaward of the reef would test it.

rows.q: Length of the oval breakwater (38 m or 46 m)
rows.model: 38 m (setting-out table of drawing 1020; the plan strip measures 38 m)
rows.stated: 46 m (drawing 1023, 23,000 + 23,000 mm between R15 and R14)
rows.diff: -8 m, about 2 % of the oval volume
rows.reason: Two drawings of the same rev C1 set disagree.
rows.resolve: The contractor's as-built setting-out table.
ev: 23,000 + 23,000 mm between SOP R15 and R14 (46 m)

rows.q: Footprint depends on the edge definition
rows.model: {{versions/lidar_2022/area_m2|n0}} m2 laser edge (default) / {{versions/design_1020/area_m2|n0}} m2 design foot / {{versions/sat_2024/area_m2|n0}} m2 photo edge
rows.stated: design drawing 1020: 6,989 m2 armour foot
rows.diff: -19 % (design) and -34 % (photo) against the default
rows.reason: Different edge definitions of the same two mounds: rock exposed at about -2.3 mODN (laser flight), the foot of the Type 4 layer (-2.15), bare rock in a photo at about -1.3 mODN. Priority survey > drawing > photo.
rows.resolve: Switch the outline version in the model header; the viewer labels each edge definition.

rows.model: z = 0 at mean sea level = +0.31 mODN (+-0.15 m, mean of four levels); slider LAT to MHWS
rows.stated: SMP2 (Aberystwyth) MHWS +2.56 / MHWN +1.06 / MLWN -0.64 / MLWS -1.74 mODN; LAT -2.44 mODN is a neighbouring-gauge value
rows.diff: HAT and the Aberystwyth chart-datum offset are not tabulated at a primary source
rows.reason: LiDAR vertical datum is not stated (ODN assumed; supported by the design crests and the flight sea surface); the flight tide (-2.3 mODN) is inferred.
rows.resolve: Admiralty / EasyTide values for Aberystwyth (REQUESTS row 6).
ev: HAT not found

rows.q: Bed under the rock is a design level
rows.model: -4.0 mODN under the north arm (derived), -3.4 under the oval centreline (derived), tail -3.0 to -3.4 (assumed)
rows.stated: drawing sections: oval -3.6 to -4.2 printed; the ground lines are schematic ('BED LEVELS VARY')
rows.reason: No measured bed under the rock exists; height and volume follow these levels.
rows.resolve: Low-tide multibeam, or a Navionics-app depth reading at the reef toe (REQUESTS rows 1-3).

rows.q: Oval is a breakwater, not a surf reef
rows.model: labelled 'BREAKWATER (oval, not a surf reef)'; the boot-shaped north mound is the SURF REEF
rows.stated: Phase 1 design: shore-parallel breakwater crest +1.50 mODN; surf reef crest +0.50 mODN
rows.reason: Both rock mounds are drawn, but only the northern one is the surf reef; the page and viewer label them differently.

rows.q: As-built flanks and the part below the water edge
rows.model: design flanks below -2.3 mODN; LiDAR surface above it
rows.stated: as built (LiDAR) 1:4.0 to 1:5.3 and 8-10 m wider than the design
rows.reason: Flanks below the LiDAR water edge are design, not measured.
rows.resolve: Low-tide imagery or multibeam of the flanks.

rows.model: not used for the model
rows.stated: Navionics shows no reef, is 0.6-1.1 m shallower than Fig 2 / EMODnet offshore; datum not stated (LAT assumed)
rows.reason: The web chart is crowd-sourced SonarChart and generalised; used only to test datums.
rows.resolve: Navionics app obstruction symbol (REQUESTS rows 1-3).

rows.model: {{versions/photo_2020-08-08/volume_m3|n0}} m3 mound envelope (photo, default) / {{versions/design_option2_2017/volume_m3|n0}} m3 (Option 2)
rows.stated: 534 containers x about 147 m3 sand = about 78,500 m3 placed (Jackson 2007 p.4; Jackson 2012 p.3; City 2020)
rows.diff: -83 % (photo) to -73 % (Option 2) against the placed volume
rows.reason: The model shows only the exposed mound seen in the photo and the 2017 multibeam (relief 1-2.5 m); containers are partly buried, stacked, displaced or lost, and the envelope includes gaps.
rows.resolve: Container-by-container multibeam or the City as-built; a post-renewal survey.

rows.model: crest -2.2 m AHD = 1.44 m below LAT (MSQ AHD = LAT + 0.760)
rows.stated: papers: -2.5 m AHD = -1.5 m LAT, i.e. AHD = LAT + 1.00
rows.reason: Two datum relations for the same design crest; the model uses MSQ because it is the official benchmark and all heights are AHD-based (only the tide levels move).
rows.resolve: The offset used in the 2018 survey (City of Gold Coast / MSQ).

rows.model: {{versions/photo_2020-08-08/area_m2|n0}} m2 visible field vs {{versions/design_option2_2017/area_m2|n0}} m2 Option 2 envelope
rows.stated: design to the -6 m contour; deeper toe to about -10 m (Jackson & Corbett 2019)
rows.diff: photo field is 45 % of the design envelope
rows.reason: The toe below about -6 m is not visible on the 2020 photo; 96.6 % of the traced arms lie inside the Option 2 envelope.
rows.resolve: Post-renewal multibeam or the 2025 State bathymetric lidar.

rows.model: 1-1.5 m (multibeam relief)
rows.stated: stage-1 estimate 4-6 m at the -6 to -8 m toe
rows.reason: The 2017 multibeam bed at the toe is -6.5 to -7.5 m and container tops are -5 to -6 m.
rows.resolve: Done 2026-10-10 (Corbett Fig 3 digitised).

rows.model: assumed smooth profile 0 / -1.8 / -2.1 m AHD at y = 0 / 100 / 190 m
rows.stated: no source resolves the surf zone here (Navionics land edge is 80 m seaward of the 2020 waterline)
rows.diff: unknown, +-1 m
rows.reason: Not part of the reef volume; affects only the look of the shore side.
rows.resolve: Navionics app and Google Earth readings (3d/REQUESTS_FOR_LIOR.md).

rows.q: Multibeam read from a colour picture
rows.model: bed and relief from Corbett Fig 3 (460 x 312 px)
rows.stated: datum and north not stated in the figure
rows.diff: +-0.4 m levels, +-10 m position
rows.reason: Hue read through a four-tick colour bar; assumed AHD and north-up.
rows.resolve: The original multibeam grid from ICM or the City.
